method: supervised warm start (Huber on depth) + DAVI (approximate value iteration); rubiks.value_scale
output: raw cost-to-go J(s) (trained without clamp); solvers use max(0, J)

stage1.loss: Huber(delta=1) of J(s) against the depth label
stage1.schedule: linear warm-up 0.05 of the steps, then cosine to 0
stage1.resume: state.pt after every completed epoch; a stop inside an epoch redoes that epoch

davi.states: fresh rubiks.sampling.random_scrambles(rng_r, batch, max_depth) on every rank r every iteration: 2 x 10000 = 20000 states per iteration (rng_r: ddp.streams)
davi.target: J'(s) = 0 if s solved; else min over all 18 moves a of 1 + J_t(a(s)), with J_t(c) = 0 if c is solved, else max(0, J_target(c))
davi.loss: MSE of the raw online output against the target
davi.optimizer: AdamW(lr=0.001, weight_decay=0.0001 on Linear weights), one step per iteration
davi.schedule: linear warm-up 0 iterations, then cosine to 0 over --davi-iters (164000, the planned horizon); a resume keeps it (exact), or changes it only with --allow-horizon-change (schedule rebuilt from the saved step: non-exact)

target_update.loss_rule: every 100 iterations since the last update: mean training loss since the last update < 0.05

probe.proxy_definition: Spearman rank correlation (average ranks for ties) between the raw J and the depth label, maximised

scale.memavailable_guard: floor 30 GiB every 5 s; 3 consecutive failed reads stop the run (memavailable-unreadable)
scale.amp: bf16 autocast over the body; head, loss, optimizer fp32
scale.emergency_save: a stop saves state.pt + last.pt with NO network evaluation (last.pt carries the last cached probe record, probe_source cached)

exit_codes.1: error, including a failed save at a stop
exit_codes.5: CUDA out of memory (state.pt not overwritten)
exit_codes.6: --ddp: the ranks diverged (ddp-divergence; state.pt not overwritten)

determinism.note: --ddp: not bit-reproducible against a single-node run (other batches; after a resume from a single-node state rank 1's stream is new); CUDA not guaranteed

ddp.batchnorm: per rank: each rank normalises with its own batch; rank 0's running statistics are broadcast at every training forward, before every target copy and at every save
ddp.gradients: fp32, averaged over the ranks by DistributedDataParallel (no compression)
ddp.update_rule: decided on the training loss averaged over the ranks; every iteration, right after the decision and before any target copy, the ranks compare the proposed decision, the iteration of the last copy and the iteration (ddp-rule-disagreement, exit 6, on a difference)
ddp.consistency: every iteration after the optimizer step and before any target copy (and before the first log point or save of a run): rank 0's batch-norm running statistics to every rank, then three exact 64-bit integer digests per tensor of the raw bits (on the device) of every rank's online state_dict, target state_dict and AdamW state, compared with rank 0's; a difference stops every rank (ddp-divergence, exit 6, no copy, log or save; nothing repaired); the mean wall time per check is check_s_mean in the metrics records
ddp.final_verdict: after the final writes (config.json, STOPPED, rank<r>-memory.jsonl) the ranks exchange their failures; a failure on any rank: exit 1 on every rank
ddp.settings: code, torch and the experiment settings arch, hidden_list, stem_list, resnet_blocks, norm, activation, weight_decay, clip, davi_batch, davi_max_depth, davi_lr, davi_warmup, target_update_loss, target_update_every, target_check_every, seed, amp, best_by, probe_per_depth, davi_iters, target_chunk, log_every, save_every, stop_at_iter, ddp_sync_bn compared across the ranks before any run file is touched (exit 2 on a difference)
ddp.streams: rank r continues its saved stream (a two-node state.pt); else rank 0 continues the stream of a single-node state.pt; else default_rng(SeedSequence(seed, spawn_key=(1, r, start iteration)))
ddp.files: rank 0 writes every run file; rank r > 0 writes only rank<r>-memory.jsonl

ranks.memavailable_guard: floor 30 GiB every 5 s; 3 consecutive failed reads stop the run (memavailable-unreadable)
